description:
Make this repository's cargo-ci checker report a load-only failure as an infrastructure fault, so that digest reuse never carries a load-induced failure across issues as a verdict.

## Background

`scripts/cargo-ci.sh` exits 1 for any failing step. Under host load, nextest test timeouts and the suite-duration budget fail on an unchanged tree, and the run is recorded `failed`, a verdict on repository content. A gate that declares inputs reuses a prior verdict over the same digest, failed ones included, so one lead's load-induced failure was reused as another issue's verdict twice on 2026-10-21 (source runs f021435e and 7000b013). After fd9bfab8, an exec checker exiting 75 records an `error` run, and an `error` run is never reused. The epic's REQ-02 requires every gate-run record to distinguish a fault from a verdict; this applies it to this repository's own cargo-ci checker. The milestone steward approved the wording below, and narrowed REQ-01 so that a quiet-host budget overrun stays a real finding against the change that crossed it.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `scripts/cargo-ci.sh` exits 75 when every failing step is environment-sensitive and the host was loaded while the suite ran: test TIMEOUT results with no FAIL result, or a suite-duration budget overrun. The run output records the observed host load and the threshold that classified it. A suite-duration overrun on a quiet host is a verdict and exits 1, as does a run that also has a failing test, a fmt or clippy failure, or a footprint budget failure.
- [hard] REQ-02: The checker's header and the cargo-ci gate description state the convention, and the gate description notes that a persistent budget overrun at low load is a real regression to investigate rather than retry.
- [hard] REQ-03: A test owns each exit path: the script's self-test or a Rust test over the classifier.

## Notes

- An `error` run never passes, so a real slowdown still blocks completion; it is rerun rather than cached.
- This edits a gate checker and the repository's gate registry; it goes through review and the gates like any task.
title: Report load-only cargo-ci failures as infrastructure faults
